drivers.variant_notes: Bally LA-4 production game ROMs (mous_u26.l4, mous_u27.l4), the pinned clone-tree parent and the driver the retained known-working table binds (cGameName = "mousn_l4"). The runtime evidence was recorded on it.

Bally LA-1 game ROMs (u26-la1.rom, u27-la1.rom) with the L-1 sound ROMs mous_u4.l1 and mous_u19.l1. Shares mousnGameData/init_mousn with the parent through CORE_CLONEDEF (pinned src/wpc/s11games.c lines 1122 and 1179-1183), and so the same GEN_S11B generation, disp16oneline display layout, A/C select relay 12, S11_MUXSW2 switch-2 copy and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) flipper wiring. Its Coil, Single Lamps and Switch Levels tests name every address exactly as LA-4 does except switch 37, which LA-1 calls "RAMP DRAIN" where LA-4 calls it "MADE LEFT RAMP" (run mousn_l1 in the variant evidence). The manual prints switch 37 as Left Ramp Exit; no source says whether that rename reflects a change on the playfield.

Bally LU-1 European game ROMs (U26 u26-la1.rom with U27 u27-lu1.rom) and the L-1 sound ROMs. Shares mousnGameData/init_mousn with the parent through CORE_CLONEDEF (pinned src/wpc/s11games.c lines 1122 and 1179-1183), and so the same GEN_S11B generation, disp16oneline display layout, A/C select relay 12, S11_MUXSW2 switch-2 copy and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) flipper wiring. Like LA-1, its service tests name every address exactly as LA-4 does except switch 37 ("RAMP DRAIN"; run mousn_lu in the variant evidence).

2019 community "LA-4C Competition MOD": patched LA-4 game ROMs (the pinned source loads the patch d87f set and keeps the patch 0a45 and f51e sets as comments; a further Rev 5.0 of October 2021 is mentioned but not loaded). Shares mousnGameData/init_mousn with the parent through CORE_CLONEDEF (pinned src/wpc/s11games.c lines 1122 and 1179-1183), and so the same GEN_S11B generation, disp16oneline display layout, A/C select relay 12, S11_MUXSW2 switch-2 copy and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) flipper wiring. Shared game data proves PinMAME routes it like the production machine; its archive is not in the local ROM corpus, so its service tests, which name every address the ROM drives, could not be compared.

TEST", lower display 08) the ROM energized 12 five times for about 1.93 s, 1.85 s apart; 0.2 s after every rise the upper display read "SELECTED C-SIDE" and the lower "C-SIDE 08", and after every fall "SELECTED A-SIDE" and "08", so the ROM reads 2 closed while 12 is energized. The Switches parts list prints "Trap 1 Up/Down". The Switches note: "Each Ball Eater has two switches. The center is #41 & #42 and tells the CPU if a ball is in the Ball Eater. The switch to the back and side is #33 & #34 and tells the CPU if the Ball Eater is up or down." Trap 1 is the right ball eater (its lamp 33 Set Trap 1 and its coils 03A and 05A stand on the right edges of the drawings) and Trap 2 the left. It is closed while the trap is down: in the gameplay run, once MOUSE TRAP was spelled, the ROM pulsed Trap 1 Up (3) while the host held 33 closed and stopped once it opened, and at power-up the ROM's ball search pulses Trap 1 Down (5) while 33 is open and Trap 1 Up instead while it is held (power-up probes). The retained script closes it when its trap goes down. In the ROM's Switch Levels test (run switch-levels) holding public 33 at 1 makes the upper display show the ROM's name for it and the lower display "06 33", so the ROM reads it active at 1. mousnGameData has no inverted-switch mask and pia4a_r returns core_getSwCol raw, so the contact the matrix sees is open at rest and closed when actuated. Projected onto the table's right trap kicker (Kicker rightTrap41), the ball eater whose up/down switch this is (part of B-20-9629); the script writes it from its trap routines (lines 615-708) and has no object for it.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,57) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. S11.VBS names this address swURFlip; its vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp write it from a staged right-flipper key only while vpmFlips.FlipperSolNumber(3) is non-zero, which core.vbs makes the default (sURFlipper = 34) unless the table calls NoUpperRightFlipper, directly or through core.vbs's cvpmFlips2.Init, which vpmInit runs and which calls it when the table defines cSingleRFlip as a number other than True. The constant does not follow the PinMAME column, and the ROM cannot read the address on this machine, so any such write has no effect.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,57) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 57 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 57: a host write to 57 is overwritten on the next update. The retained known-working script drives it: MousinAround_KeyDown and MousinAround_KeyUp pass the right flipper key to S11.VBS vpmKeyDown/vpmKeyUp (script lines 244 and 260), which set Controller.Switch(swLRFlip) with swLRFlip = 82 (excerpt vpm-script-library-flippers). In the Switch Levels run holding this address showed "RIGHT FLIPPER" and "06 57". The physical counterpart is the right cabinet flipper switch, which fires the flipper coil through the flipper circuit and is read by the CPU at its matrix address.

mechanisms.behavior: A drained ball rests on the outhole switch (9) and the Outhole Kicker (1, B-8039-2, AE-23-800) kicks it into the trough, where up to three balls queue on Trough 3 (13, left), Trough 2 (12, middle) and Trough 1 (11, right; the ROM calls 11-13 TROUGH 1-3 BALL(S)). The Ball Shooter Lane Feeder (2, C-9638-1, AE-23-800) kicks the lead ball into the shooter lane (14). In the gameplay run the ROM fed the first ball 0.42 s after game-on rose and kicked the outhole 0.56 s after 9 closed. With the trough empty at power-up the ROM runs a ball search through 1, 5, 8, 11, 14 and 16; with all three trough switches held it runs none. The retained script models the trough as one three-ball cvpmBallStack.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: A Trap (Ball Eater) Assembly (B-20-9629: the 20-9629 Ball Eater, an AE-26-1400 coil and an SM1-28-800 coil) on the right side. Trap 1 Up (3, AE-26-1400) raises the ball eater and Trap 1 Down (5, SM1-28-800) lowers it; switch 33 closes while it is down and switch 41 reports a ball in it. The rules: spelling M-O-U-S-E T-R-A-P sets the traps that lock the balls, two balls are trapped and the third releases them when it is put into play (Multi-ball); after Multi-ball the traps stay up and must trap the mice again for the Jackpot. In the gameplay run, once MOUSE TRAP was spelled, the ROM pulsed the up coil about every 0.8 s while 33 stayed closed and stopped once it opened; at power-up the ball search pulses the down coil while 33 is open. The retained script raises the trap with 3 and kicks out a ball resting in it, and lowers it with 5.
mechanisms.label: Trap 1 (right ball eater)

mechanisms.behavior: The second B-20-9629 ball eater, on the left side: Trap 2 Up (4, AE-26-1400) raises it, Trap 2 Down (8, SM1-28-800) lowers it, switch 34 closes while it is down and 42 reports a ball in it. It behaves as Trap 1 in every run.
mechanisms.label: Trap 2 (left ball eater)

mechanisms.behavior: Three center targets (29-31) on a motorized bank that the Motor Relay (11, 5580-12145-01) raises and lowers. Two limit switches on the motor (5647-12073-06) report its ends: 43 when the bank is up (the Switches note's left side switch) and 50 when it is down (the right side switch). The rules: hitting the center targets in sequence lowers the targets and lights the kickback. The retained table puts the Center Ramp switch (35) directly behind the bank, and its script makes the targets and a wall behind them non-collidable while the bank is down. The ROM releases the relay once the limit it is waiting for closes: in the gameplay run the third target energized it and it released 0.27 s after 50 closed, and the mouse hole lock energized it again; the Motor Bank Test raises and lowers the bank, released the relay 0.09 s after 50 and 0.08 s after 43 closed, and shows an error when a limit does not close ("DN 01 ERROR" after 7.6 s without 50, "00 ERROR" after 15.2 s with neither). The retained script moves the three target primitives over about 2 s each way and writes 43 and 50 at the ends.
mechanisms.label: Motorized center target bank

mechanisms.behavior: A shot enters the mouse hole past Mouse Hole Enter (32) and queues on Mouse Hole Lock 1-3 (59-61, part of C-13061) on the back panel; the Mouse Hole Exit (16, the B-13081 Drop Kick Mech. Assembly with an AE-26-1200 coil and the B-13082 ball tray) releases a ball. The rules: completing C-H-E-E-S-E opens the mouse hole to build the Jackpot, sending the last mouse home to the mouse hole after Multi-ball collects it, and spelling MILLION opens it for 1,000,000 points. In the gameplay run the ROM fired 16 0.93 s after 59 closed; with 59 held from power-up it fired it six times about 1.8 s apart. The retained script holds the ball in its MouseHole kicker while 59 is set.
mechanisms.label: Mouse hole lock and drop kick (back panel)

mechanisms.behavior: The Ball Deflector (Diverter) C-12902-1 with its B-12858 Diverter Mech. Assembly: an AE-23-800 coil drives the A-12957-1 D/A shaft actuator through a flat cam, and the A-12953 Mini Switch (49) reports the diverter's position. The retained script names it SolMouseHoleDiverter: each pulse swings its arm, toggles switch 49 and with it which of two walls (WallDiverter or WallGuideToTop) is solid. At power-up with an empty trough the ball search pulses 14 seven times, three with 49 held.
mechanisms.label: Ball diverter

mechanisms.behavior: A kickback (13, AE-24-900, "Kickback (L Outlane)") in the left outlane, whose switch (51) the ROM calls "KICKBACK". Lamp 36 (Kickback) shows it lit; the rules light it when the center targets lower. In the gameplay run the ROM fired 13 0.012 s after 51 closed. The retained script enables its Kickback kicker while 13 is on.
mechanisms.label: Left outlane kickback

mechanisms.behavior: The Top Lanes Gate (22, Special #6, SM2-35-4000; the ROM's Coil Test calls it "SHOOTER GATE") above the three top lanes (22-24). The rules: a plunger skill shot through the lit top lanes scores 100,000 times the ball number, and completing the top lanes earns the 2X and 3X bonus multipliers. In the gameplay run the ROM energized the gate 2.8 s after the first ball was served and held it until ball 2 was being served. The retained script opens its GateTopRight while 22 is on.
mechanisms.label: Top lanes gate

mechanisms.behavior: Three jet bumpers in the upper centre: Left (17, switch 52), Right (19, switch 53) and Lower (21, switch 54), each with an AE-23-800 coil and an SW-11A-37 skirt switch. They are special solenoids, but mousnGameData maps no switch to them in PinMAME: the ROM fires each through its PIA line, 0.001-0.004 s after its switch closed in the gameplay run, so a consumer drives only the switch.
mechanisms.label: Three jet bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Two B-12665 slingshot kickers above the flippers (AE-26-1500 coils): Left (18) with switch 55 and Right (20) with 56, each address carrying an SW-1A-114 kicker switch and an SW-1A-120 score switch. In PinMAME the ROM fires each special solenoid itself, 0.014-0.015 s after its switch closed in the gameplay run.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: Two flippers with FL11630/50VDC coils (the Solenoid Table's spelling; the list prints "Fl 11630/50VDC"). The cabinet flipper switches fire the coils through the flipper circuit, so no Sol. No. or driver is printed for them and PinMAME fabricates 45-48 from the buttons at public 82 and 84; the CPU reads the switches at 58 (left) and 57 (right), which core_updateSw copies from 84 and 82.
mechanisms.label: Two flippers, cabinet-wired

mechanisms.behavior: The A/C Select Relay (12) on the Aux Power Driver Board switches the solenoid supply between the "A" and "C" terminals so that each of the eight switched drivers (Q22-Q25, Q30-Q33) serves an "A" coil while it is released and a "C" flasher while it is energized. Pinned PinMAME publishes the C loads separately at 25-32 and copies the relay's state into switch 2, the C-side switch the ROM checks in its C-Side test.
mechanisms.label: A/C solenoid select relay

mechanisms.behavior: The A-side load of pair 07 (7, AE-23-800) raps the B-10686-1 Knocker Assembly.
mechanisms.label: Knocker

physical.notes: Solenoid Table entry 01A ("Outhole Kicker"); the Solenoid/Flashers list prints "Outhole". Switched pair 01A/01C on driver Q33: the "A" load is pulsed with the A/C Select Relay (12) de-energized and the "C" load with it energized (the table's note 3). Pinned updsol publishes the A load at 1 and the C load at 25. The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 1 of 30 while the upper display shows "OUTHOLE". In the gameplay run the ROM fired it 0.56 s after the drained ball closed the outhole switch (9); with 9 held from power-up it fired ten times in 12 s, and with no ball anywhere the ROM's ball search pulses it twice (power-up probes). Retained script: SolOuthole (line 304), bsTrough.SolIn, which kicks a drained ball from Kicker Drain into the trough. Placed at the retained table's Kicker Drain, a documented projection onto the drain kicker the script's ball stack receives balls on; the B-8039-2 outhole kicker coil has no object of its own.

Solenoid Table entry 09 ("Insert Board Gnl Illum Relay"); the Solenoid/Flashers list prints "Insert Bd. Gen. Illum.". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 17 of 30 while the upper display shows "INSERT G.I.". The retained script has no callback for this address. The insert-board G.I. relay (5580-09555-01 on Relay Board C-11998-1, the table's note 4a). Pinned PinMAME types it as a reverse-acting #44 "Backbox GI output", so energized means the insert-board general illumination is off.

Solenoid Table entry 10 ("Playfield Gnl Illum Relay"); the Solenoid/Flashers list prints "Playfield Gen. Illum.". Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 18 of 30 while the upper display shows "PLAYFIELD G.I.". Retained script: SolGI (line 311), which turns the table's G.I. off while the solenoid is on (lines 1188-1204). The playfield G.I. relay (5580-09555-01 on Relay Board C-11998-1, the table's note 4a). Energized means G.I. off: pinned PinMAME types it as a reverse-acting #44 "Playfield GI output" and the retained script's SolGI(IsOff) turns its G.I. off while it is on. This record cites no G.I. bulb list or layout from the manual; the placements are the bulb under each light of the retained table's GIBulbs collection and the bulb-mesh light in each jet bumper cap (GIBumperLights). A table's G.I. grouping is not the machine's wiring, so these placements stay observed and no quantity is asserted.

Solenoid Table entry 11 ("Motor Relay"). Solenoid Type "Controlled". The ROM's Coil Test (run coil-test) pulses this address at step 19 of 30 while the upper display shows "STANDUP MOTOR". In the gameplay run the third center target (31) energized it 0.025 s later and it released 0.27 s after the host closed the bank-down switch 50; the closure of mouse hole lock 1 (59) energized it again 0.49 s later. In the Motor Bank Test it released 0.09 s after the host closed 50 and 0.08 s after the host closed 43, and with neither switch closing it stayed on for 15.2 s before the display read "00 ERROR". At power-up with an empty trough the ROM ran it for 7.6-7.9 s at a time while neither limit changed (power-up probes). Retained script: SolMotorBank (line 312), which moves the three center target primitives down from the up limit or up from the down limit over about 2 s, opening the limit it leaves and closing 50 or 43 at the far end (lines 751-821). The Motor Relay (5580-12145-01 on Relay Board C-11902-1, the table's note 4b) switches the motor that raises and lowers the three center targets; the ROM's Coil Test calls it "STANDUP MOTOR". The same relay output lowers and raises the bank: in the Motor Bank Test one span ended when 50 closed and the next, shown as "UP", when 43 closed. Placed at the retained table's Primitive pTarget30, the bank's middle target (object position), a documented projection onto the motorized bank's middle target; the motor and its relay sit under the playfield and have no object of their own.
